# Causality Reference

> Every causal edge, reason code, sync outcome and error type JIM's synchronisation engine can record, generated from the enums themselves.

**The source of truth is the code, not this page.** This reference is generated by reading `src/JIM.Models/Activities/CausalEdgeEnums.cs`, `src/JIM.Models/Activities/ActivityEnums.cs` and `src/JIM.Models/Activities/ActivityRunProfileExecutionItemErrorType.cs` directly; if this page and the enums ever disagree, the enums win and this page is stale. Regenerate the affected table by re-reading the enum and its ordinal test rather than hand-editing a row.

## The append-only rule

All four enums below are **persisted by ordinal** on Run Profile Execution Items and causal edge rows, and those rows are the permanent audit record of what synchronisation did and why. Inserting a member in the middle, or reordering two, silently relabels every historical row already in a customer's database: a run that projected an object could read back as having deleted it, and nothing would fail at the point of the mistake. Every one of these enums is therefore **append-only**: a new member always goes at the end, never in the middle, and an existing member's underlying value is never reused or changed.

This is enforced by four dedicated ordinal-pinning test fixtures in `test/JIM.Models.Tests/Activities/`, each holding a `Dictionary<TEnum, int>` of every member's expected ordinal:

| Enum | Ordinal test |
|---|---|
| `CausalEdgeType`, `CausalReasonCode` | `CausalEdgeOrdinalTests.cs` |
| `ActivityRunProfileExecutionItemSyncOutcomeType` | `SyncOutcomeTypeOrdinalTests.cs` |
| `ActivityRunProfileExecutionItemErrorType` | `ErrorTypeOrdinalTests.cs` |

Adding a member is expected and welcome; add it to the end of the enum and add its ordinal to the matching test's map in the same change. Never edit an existing entry in either place.

## How the portal renders these

Two independent rendering pipelines cover these enums, and they do not overlap:

- **Sync outcomes and causal edges** (the causality Lineage/Timeline views, `src/JIM.Web/Shared/Causality/`) go through `src/JIM.Web/Causality/`:
  - **`OutcomeDisplayMap`** is the single source of truth for how every `ActivityRunProfileExecutionItemSyncOutcomeType` value is displayed: a plain-English label, a `CausalityTone` (Success/Info/Warning/Error/Primary/Secondary) and a Material icon. Every one of the 52 members below has an entry; an unmapped future value falls back to the bare enum name rather than throwing. `OutcomeDisplayMapVocabularyTests` (JIM.Web.Tests) asserts every label against the product-noun rules (no "MVO"/"CSO"/"Identity"/"record").
  - **`CausalityModelBuilder`** places each outcome into a lane (Source, Downstream or Identity) for the visualisation's columns, and turns each `CausalEdgeType`/`CausalReasonCode` pair recorded on a `CausalEdge` row into a node in the model.
  - **`CausalityCauseWording`** renders the plain-English sentence for a cross-item causal edge (a `CausalEdgeType` plus its `CausalReasonCode`): "X rejected the generated value as already in use, so JIM generated a new one", and so on. This is the only one of the four builder types that reads `CausalReasonCode` at all; reason codes never appear directly in `OutcomeDisplayMap`.
  - **`CausalitySummaryBuilder`** composes the Activity's plain-English summary band from groups of outcomes (for example, folding every `GeneratedValueAssigned`/`GeneratedValueAdopted` event on a run into one clause via `BuildGeneratedValueClauses`).
- **RPEI errors** (`ActivityRunProfileExecutionItemErrorType`) are a separate pipeline and do **not** go through any of the four types above: `src/JIM.Web/Helpers.cs`'s `ErrorPhaseTitles` dictionary supplies the heading shown above an error ("Import Rejected", "Synchronisation Failed", "Export Refused", and so on, grouped by which phase of the run the failure belongs to), consumed directly by `ActivityDetail.razor`, `ActivityRunProfileExecutionItemDetail.razor`, `ActivityItemPendingExportPanel.razor` and `CausalityPanel.razor`. `ErrorPhaseTitleTests` asserts every member has an entry.

## `CausalEdgeType`

`src/JIM.Models/Activities/CausalEdgeEnums.cs`. Only hops that cross a Run Profile Execution Item or Activity boundary get an edge; a hop within one item is already a causal structure (a sync outcome tree) and must not get a duplicate one. 5 members.

| Ordinal | Member | Meaning | Produced by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `MetaverseObjectDeletionCausedDeprovision` | A Metaverse Object deletion caused a delete-type Pending Export to be staged against one of the object's own provisioned Connected System Objects, when the export could not be recorded under the deletion's own outcome and became a standalone item. | `SyncTaskProcessorBase` (deletion handling) |
| 1 | `MetaverseObjectDeletionCausedReferenceRemoval` | A Metaverse Object deletion caused reference recall to stage a Pending Export removing a reference to it from another object. The only edge where cause and effect sit on two different objects. | `SyncTaskProcessorBase` (reference recall) |
| 2 | `ExportCausedImportConfirmation` | An executed export caused the confirming outcome recorded on the next import. Needed because reconciliation correlates only by Connected System Object id, and an object can cycle through export and import repeatedly. | `SyncImportTaskProcessor` (confirming import) |
| 3 | `PendingExportQueueingCausedExportExecution` | The synchronisation that staged a Pending Export caused the export run that carried it out; the two sit in different Activities, so the executing item has no other way to say why it exported anything. | `SyncExportTaskProcessor` (queueing-to-execution correlation) |
| 4 | `ExportRejectionCausedGeneratedValueRevision` 🆕 UVG | Unique Value Generation (#242): an export run's rejection of a generated value caused the next synchronisation to revise the value (import mode) and re-stage the export. | **Unique Value Generation.** Release 4 (Collision Remediation, Phase 8), not yet implemented: `SyncExportTaskProcessor` does not yet write this edge (no `UniqueValueAlreadyInUse` handling exists in it today). The ordinal exists because Phase 1 appended every planned enum member up front. |

## Unique Value Generation (#242) at a glance

🆕 UVG marks twelve members across all four enums, added in Phase 1 of the [Unique Value Generation plan](plans/doing/UNIQUE_VALUE_GENERATION.md) so the ordinal tests changed exactly once for the whole feature rather than once per release. Their wiring status differs by release, and is **not** uniform, which is the one place this feature's enum footprint needs reading carefully rather than assumed from the enum comments alone:

| Release | Members | Wired today? |
|---|---|---|
| 1 (generation and tokens) | `SyncOutcomeType.GeneratedValueAssigned`, `.GeneratedValueAdopted`; `ErrorType.GeneratedValueExhausted`, `.GeneratedValueWidthExceeded` | Yes: produced by `SyncTaskProcessorBase.ResolvePendingGeneratedValuesAsync` and `ResolveExportGeneratedValuesAsync`. |
| 1, reused early | `ErrorType.GeneratedValueCollisionUnresolved` | Yes, but for `GenerationOutcomeKind.AdoptionConflict` (a release-1 adopt-before-generate race), not the release-4 anchored-rejection case its own XML doc comment and the PRD describe. Re-check this when Phase 8 lands: it may gain a second call site rather than being newly wired. |
| 2 (retired values register) | `SyncOutcomeType.GeneratedValueRetired` | No. `RetiredGeneratedValue` and its register do not exist in the codebase yet (Phase 6). |
| 4 (Collision Remediation) | `SyncOutcomeType.GeneratedValueRemediated`; `CausalEdgeType.ExportRejectionCausedGeneratedValueRevision`; `CausalReasonCode.GeneratedValueAlreadyInUse`, `.GeneratedValueAnchoredElsewhere`, `.GeneratedValueRenameAuthorised` | No. `SyncExportTaskProcessor` has no handling for `ConnectedSystemExportErrorType.UniqueValueAlreadyInUse` yet (Phase 8). |

Two adjacent, non-causal enums complete the picture but are not persisted-by-ordinal causal state, so they sit outside the tables above: `PendingExportStatus.Parked` (the NeedsDecision holding status for a Pending Export, release 4) and `ConnectedSystemExportErrorType.UniqueValueAlreadyInUse` (the export-side classification a connector reports before any of this feature's causal members come into play). Neither has a dedicated ordinal test; `PendingExportStatus` and `ConnectedSystemExportErrorType` sit outside the causality model's own append-only contract, even though good practice still keeps both append-only in fact.

## Verifying this page

Every table above was generated by reading the enum source files and the `OutcomeDisplayMap` / `Helpers.ErrorPhaseTitles` dictionaries directly, not from memory or the plan documents. To re-verify after a change:

1. Diff the enum file against this page's ordinal column; a member added anywhere but the end, or a renumbering, is a bug this page cannot catch (the ordinal tests can).
2. Run the four ordinal test fixtures (`test/JIM.Models.Tests/Activities/CausalEdgeOrdinalTests.cs`, `SyncOutcomeTypeOrdinalTests.cs`, `ErrorTypeOrdinalTests.cs`) to confirm the persisted ordinals themselves have not drifted.
3. For "produced by" and "wired today" claims specifically: grep the worker and application layers for the member's fully-qualified name (`OutcomeType.MemberName`, `ErrorType.MemberName`) rather than trusting an XML doc comment's stated intent; a member can be declared and documented (as several Unique Value Generation members are) well before anything actually writes it.
